note: Public eulogies for VAULTED projects. We preserve them for IP, lineage, and the lessons. Add new entries here; /vault/tombstones/ renders them in order.

tombstones.name: DreadSpike
tombstones.epitaph: The first sky-arc. A world too small to hold its own myth.
lessons: Saga scope must match sustainable production cadence.
Naming a universe after one event constrains its room to grow.
An ending is part of an IP — Voidfall inherits DreadSpike's bones cleanly because we honored them.

tombstones.name: Gridiron GM Play
tombstones.epitaph: The playable web build that proved the loop worked. Forged the audience that's waiting for the next one.
lessons: Shipping a playable v0 beats shipping a polished v1 — the v0 told us which 3 systems to deepen.
A vaulted game is a contract: Return Notice replaces Early Access for re-engagement.
Founder-tier members get the comeback first — proves the membership promise.

tombstones.name: VaultSpark Football GM
tombstones.epitaph: Renamed to Franchise Architect. The studio-prefixed, sport-locked name retired — the deep front-office engine, and every save, ranking, and leaderboard, carried straight over.
lessons: A name that leads with the studio and locks to one sport can't grow into a franchise — Franchise Architect can, across every sport to come.
Rebrand the shell, keep the engine: the loop that earned the audience shipped forward untouched.
A public rename is a promotion with a paper trail, not a quiet reset.

tombstones.name: CryptoMatrix Pro
tombstones.epitaph: Pivoted and relaunched as Velaxis. The brand died; the engine lived.
lessons: A brand can be vaulted without losing the technology underneath.
Telling the lineage publicly ("became Velaxis") makes a vault honest, not a failure.
Two years of trading-tool research compress into one paragraph — and that's enough.
